validity.researcher_notes: The line is real. Ukrainian Wikipedia, Ukrtransgaz's own history, an archived Ukrainian encyclopedia article and a 2020 Russian tender all name it, and none depends on the GEM wiki. It is a 1220 mm trunk line from Tula in Russia to Kyiv, built for Yamburg gas. It is correctly a transmission line. It runs next to Dashava-Kyiv-Bryansk-Moscow (P1465) and the Yelets-Kursk-Kyiv line (P0776) but is a separate pipe with its own length and diameter. Caveat: Russian transit ended in January 2025, and no 2024 or later source says this line is still in use.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: No source dated 2024 or later was found that says this line is in use or idle. The newest line-specific item is a March 2020 Russian tender to decommission a metering site on the Russian side. Russian transit through Ukraine ended on 1 January 2025. The Ukrainian section may still carry domestic or reverse flows, but this is not documented. Status stays operating on the sheet. Absence of news is not evidence of closure.
